summary: This roadmap proves the Gross–Stark leading-term formula for a totally odd finite-order character of a totally real field at every rational prime, including two. It develops the signed p-adic regulator, cyclotomic cohomology and orthogonality, weight-one cuspidal families, three infinitesimal Hecke quotients, the arithmetic specialization of shared Galois extension machinery, and the determinant comparison. Exact analytic order in arbitrary rank remains equivalent to regulator nonvanishing.

nodes.title: Gross–Stark arithmetic data
nodes.statement: Fix a totally real number field F, a rational prime p (including 2), algebraic embeddings into C and C_p, and a continuous finite-order totally odd character χ of G_F. Put H=F̄^{ker χ}, G=Gal(H/F), and choose a finite extension E/Q_p containing the embedded values of χ. H/F is cyclic CM, χ is faithful on G, and its complex conjugation c satisfies χ(c)=−1. For a finite prime q, χ(q) is its arithmetic-Frobenius value when unramified and is 0 when ramified. Partition the primes above p into R={q:χ(q)=1} and R′; put r=|R|. This packages the supplied character and prime carriers without replacing them.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
All χ-components use χ^{-1}; E has characteristic zero even when p=2.
proofSteps: Use the supplied ray-class/Galois character correspondence and finite-image quotient.
Total oddness makes the fixed field of complex conjugation totally real and H totally imaginary.
Use faithfulness to identify χ(q)=1 with complete splitting in H/F.
acceptance: Every q above p belongs to exactly one part; χ and χ^{-1} have the same R.

sources.match: The arithmetic setting and the exceptional Euler-factor partition fix the scope of the theorem.

nodes.title: Odd p-units and divisor components
nodes.statement: Let U=O_H[1/p]^× and X=⊕_{P|p} Z·[P], with their natural G-actions. In additive notation set U^-={u:c(u)=−u} and X^-={x:c(x)=−x}; multiplicatively the first equation is c(u)=u^{-1}. Define U_χ and X_χ as the χ^{-1}-eigenspaces of U^-⊗_Z E and X^-⊗_Z E. The character projector on either rationalized G-module is e_χ=|G|^{-1}∑_g χ(g)g. Define o_p(u)=(ord_P(u))_P and the signed map ℓ_p(u)=(−log_p N_{H_P/Q_p}(u))_P, extended E-linearly and restricted to the χ-components.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
Use the supplied Iwasawa logarithm with log_p(p)=0, not the unextended principal-unit series.
Tensor products use Additive U; all inverses of 2 and |G| occur only after extension to E.
proofSteps: Form the localization-unit carrier and the free divisor module on the supplied finite prime set.
Valuations and local norm logarithms are additive and G-equivariant; therefore they restrict to minus and χ-parts.
For a prime outside R the corresponding permutation module has zero χ^{-1}-part; the spanning consequence is proved with the valuation isomorphism.
acceptance: No integral minus-idempotent claim is used at p=2.
The codomain of both restricted maps is the same X_χ.

nodes.title: Valuation isomorphism and rank
nodes.statement: The map o_p:U^-⊗Q→X^-⊗Q is an isomorphism of Q[G]-modules. Consequently o_p^χ:U_χ→X_χ is an E-linear equivalence and dim_E U_χ=dim_E X_χ=r. For chosen primes P_i above the distinct q_i∈R and any E-basis u_j of U_χ, O=(ord_{P_i}(u_j)) has nonzero determinant. Ordinary units of the CM field have zero odd component after tensoring with Q. The χ-projections of units supported above R span U_χ.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: By the existing Dirichlet unit rank theorem, the units of H and of its totally real fixed field H⁺ have equal rational rank. The injection of H⁺ units therefore spans the rationalized H units, so c acts as the identity and their odd component is zero. This identifies the kernel of the odd valuation map.
The class group is finite, so a positive multiple of each prime divisor is principal; rationalization makes the valuation map onto, including on odd parts.

Decompose the prime permutation module by decomposition groups. Faithfulness gives a one-dimensional χ^{-1}-summand exactly for q∈R and zero otherwise. Apply the same rational divisor argument to the R_H-unit subgroup to obtain the spanning assertion.
acceptance: This is an isomorphism of rationalized odd modules, not of the full integral p-unit and divisor groups.
The rank-zero map is the unique equivalence between zero vector spaces.

sources.match: The rational valuation isomorphism and the component dimension imply the nonzero valuation determinant.

nodes.title: Gross’s p-adic regulator
nodes.statement: Define R_p(χ)=det_E(ℓ_p^χ∘(o_p^χ)^{-1}) as an endomorphism of X_χ. For a choice of P_i|q_i∈R let o_i=ord_{P_i} and let ℓ_i=log_p N_{F_{q_i}/Q_p}; the complete splitting identifies H_{P_i}=F_{q_i}. If O=(o_i(u_j)) and L=(ℓ_i(u_j)), then R_p(χ)=det(−L)/det(O). The zero-dimensional determinant is 1. The value is independent of the ordered primes and unit basis and commutes with extension of E.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
The maps ℓ_i are unsigned; the endomorphism uses the signed ℓ_p.
O is invertible by the preceding theorem.
proofSteps: Apply Mathlib LinearMap.det to the endomorphism of the finite-dimensional E-space X_χ.
Use the coordinate map X_χ≅E^r from the chosen primes, then the matrix is (−L)O^{-1}.
Matrix determinant multiplicativity proves the ratio, basis invariance and covariance under changing prime lifts.
acceptance: Changing a prime lift rescales the corresponding O and L rows by the same nonzero character value.
A singular logarithm matrix is permitted and gives regulator zero.

sources.match: The invariant determinant and its coordinate ratio determine the sign and the choice-independent regulator.

nodes.title: Analytic leading terms
nodes.statement: Use the supplied complex Artin L-function and its p-depletion L*(χ,z)=L(χ,z)∏_{q|p}(1−χ(q)(Nq)^{-z}), and the supplied Deligne–Ribet branch f_χ(z)=L_p(χω,z), with f_χ(n)=L*(χω^n,n) for integers n≤0. Put D_χ=L(χ,0)∏_{q∈R′}(1−χ(q))≠0 and L_an(χ)=f_χ^{(r)}(0)/(r!D_χ). For its finite analytic order s set L*_an(χ)=f_χ^{(s)}(0)/(s!D_χ)≠0. These definitions use the branch χω in every derivative. Complex L*(χ,z) has order r at zero.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
The germ is analytic at zero, including the exceptional branch χ=ω^{-1}: its possible pole is at s=1, and its pole-clearing factor is a unit near zero.
For p=2 use ω:Z_2^×→{±1} and principal part in 1+4Z_2.
proofSteps: Import the supplied critical values, algebraicity, interpolation and nonvanishing at zero.
Each exceptional Euler factor has a simple complex zero, whereas the other factors and L(χ,0) are nonzero.
Analytic Taylor coefficients give the factorial normalization; interpolation at nonzero critical values makes the analytic germ nonzero and s finite.
acceptance: When s>r, L_an=0; when s=r, L_an=L*_an.
The removed Euler factors in D_χ are exactly R′, not all primes above p.

nodes.title: All-prime lower bound for the order
nodes.statement: For every prime p, including 2, ord_{z=0} L_p(χω,z)≥r. Prove it by the Charollois–Dasgupta/Spiess analytic route: after one auxiliary smoothing prime c away from fp with 1−χ(c)Nc≠0, the smoothed branch is an analytic unit times f_χ; its first r Taylor coefficients vanish. This is an inequality, with no assumption of regulator nonvanishing or exact order.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
Use the same χ, Euler factors and dyadic sign branch as in the analytic invariant.
proofSteps: Choose c by the ray-class/prime correspondence so the smoothing factor is nonzero at zero. Use the supplier’s Eisenstein-cocycle realization of that smoothed Deligne–Ribet measure and its Mellin identity.

For r exceptional primes, choose totally positive π_i generating positive powers of their ray ideal classes. Set T=⟨π_i⟩ and U=E_+×T. In the space C_c^♭ of compactly supported functions constant near zero in exceptional coordinates, the induced-function decomposition of CD14 Lemma 5.3 makes this a free C_p[T]-module. Thus H_q(T,C_c^♭)=0 for q>0, and the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence gives the edge isomorphism of Theorem 5.1. These homological steps have no odd-prime assumption.

CD14 Theorem 5.2: for k<r, expand (∑ℓ_q(x_q))^k. In each monomial an exceptional coordinate is absent; the difference (1−π_i) on the corresponding box writes it in the T-augmentation ideal, with lower-degree errors handled inductively. Its homology class therefore vanishes.

Pair with the supplied measure cocycle to obtain vanishing of derivatives of orders k<r (CD14 (79)–(84)). Divide by the smoothing unit. The main-conjecture alternative from the parent I.5 applies only at odd p and is not used for p=2.
acceptance: The source’s dyadic replacement μ_{p−1}→{±1} is retained.
At r=0 the assertion is vacuous and does not assert a zero.

sources.match: The smoothed analytic order bound is proved by an augmentation-ideal vanishing argument valid also for p=2.
The known lower bound is a separate input to the leading-term proof.

nodes.title: Two Gross conjectures and their boundary
nodes.statement: Distinguish the exact-order assertion ord_0 f_χ=r from the leading-term assertion L_an(χ)=R_p(χ). The latter is the theorem proved in GS.5; conditional on the latter, the former is equivalent to R_p(χ)≠0 by the lower bound. GS.5 supplies that hypothesis. No general exact-order or regulator-nonvanishing theorem is asserted. The characteristic polynomial of ℓ_p^χ(o_p^χ)^{-1} is an available linear-algebra object; the conjectural formulas for all its coefficients are outside the endpoint here.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: Use the analytic Taylor coefficient criterion and the lower bound.
A nonzero rank-r coefficient is equivalent to exact order r.
Keep the higher characteristic-polynomial statement explicitly conjectural; only its determinant coefficient is supplied by the endpoint.
acceptance: The zero-regulator case must remain compatible with a strictly larger analytic order.

sources.match: The leading-term equality and exact-order conjecture are different assertions; the characteristic-polynomial extension is contextual.

nodes.title: Restricted continuous cohomology
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional topological E-vector space V with scalar G_F-action χ^{-1}, let H_R^1(G_F,V(χ^{-1})) be the subspace of continuous H^1 whose restriction to H^1(I_q,V(χ^{-1})) is zero at every finite q∉R. Use the existing continuous cocycle quotient, with cocycle κ(gh)=κ(g)+χ^{-1}(g)κ(h) and coboundary (χ^{-1}(g)−1)v. At q∈R the action is trivial, so a local class is a continuous homomorphism F_q^× completed profinitely→V through Serre reciprocity. On E coefficients, o_q and ℓ_q span a two-dimensional local subspace.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
Choose compatible decomposition embeddings at every finite prime.
The local reciprocity convention sends rec(ϖ^{-1}) to arithmetic Frobenius, and on units the cyclotomic character is the norm; invert a supplier’s Artin map if needed.
proofSteps: Use the existing H^1 carrier, restriction and twisted scalar action. Form the intersection of the kernels of all inertia restriction maps.
At q∈R, χ|G_q=1 by complete splitting. Apply the baseline trivial-action identification and the supplied absolute local reciprocity map.

The valuation and the norm logarithm are continuous and extend to the profinite multiplicative completion. Their independence follows from a deep principal unit with nonzero norm logarithm and a uniformizer of valuation 1.
acceptance: The coefficients have their p-adic vector topology, never a discrete topology.
Unramified means zero inertia class; a representative need not vanish on inertia where the action is nontrivial.

sources.match: Restricted continuous classes and their local reciprocity realizations are the setting of both orthogonality proofs.

nodes.title: Kummer description of the dual local condition
nodes.statement: The rationalized Kummer map identifies U_χ with the subgroup of H^1(G_F,E(χ)(1)) with local unit-Kummer condition at every finite q∉R. Locally it identifies (lim_n H_P^×/(H_P^×)^{p^n})⊗_{Z_p}E with H^1(G_{H_P},E(1)), using the additive form of the multiplicative completion; at q∉R the class is in the local condition orthogonal to the unramified condition on E(χ^{-1}). With the pairing ordered as H^1(E(χ^{-1})) first and H^1(E(χ)(1)) second, the cup-product/invariant pairing with the Kummer image of u is a fixed universal sign times evaluation at u under the chosen reciprocity convention.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
Inverse limits are formed before inverting p; do not replace the p-adic completion of units by the uncompleted group.
proofSteps: Apply the supplier’s finite S-unit Kummer sequence for p^n, pass to inverse limits with its class-group torsion correction, then tensor with E; finiteness of the class group removes the correction.
Use finite-index descent along H/F: |G| is invertible in E, so restriction identifies the χ^{-1}-component.
Ordinary CM units have zero odd component. At nonexceptional p-primes the valuation component also vanishes, yielding exactly the R-local dual condition.
Transport the supplier’s local evaluation/cup-product identity through the chosen inverse Artin normalization, keeping one universal sign.
acceptance: At a finite coefficient level the class-group term is present; it disappears only after the stated rationalization.
The same pairing order is used in the global invariant sum and in the evaluation identity.
At primes above p, the dual unit-Kummer condition is stated as such; it is not confused with ordinary unramifiedness of E(χ)(1).

sources.match: The global and local Kummer maps identify the dual Selmer subgroup and turn local Tate pairings into evaluations.
The rank-one Kummer and duality calculation generalizes by retaining all exceptional local factors.

nodes.title: Orthogonality from Poitou–Tate duality
nodes.statement: For κ∈H_R^1(G_F,V(χ^{-1})) and u∈U_χ, ∑_{i=1}^r (res_{q_i}κ)(u)=0 in V. This holds for every finite-dimensional V. The evaluation uses the chosen prime P_i and the local norm/reciprocity identifications.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: First take V=E and the Kummer class of u. The rational Poitou–Tate invariant sum is zero.
At q∉R the paired local Selmer conditions annihilate one another. At q∈R the local pairing is the same universal sign times evaluation, so the common sign cancels from the zero sum.
Choose a basis of V, apply the scalar result to each continuous coordinate map, and recombine. Real dyadic Tate corrections vanish after tensoring with E.
acceptance: For r=0 the sum is empty and equals zero.
No ordering switch of the two cup-product arguments occurs mid-proof.

nodes.title: Orthogonality from global reciprocity
nodes.statement: The same sum ∑_i(res_{q_i}κ)(u) is zero by a class-field-theoretic proof independent of Poitou–Tate. proofSteps: Finite-group cohomology in positive degree vanishes over E; inflation–restriction therefore gives the equivariant homomorphism description.
For a global R_H-unit, its principal idele has trivial global Artin image. Away from R_H its components are units whose inertia evaluations vanish.
Sum local evaluations over primes above q_i, then project by e_χ; equivariance gives a common nonzero scalar multiple of the sum over the selected P_i. Divide by that scalar in E.
Use the spanning of U_χ by χ-projected R_H-units and E-linearity.

It gives a continuous homomorphism of the everywhere-unramified abelian Galois group of H to a torsion-free E-vector space. The relevant class-field quotient is finite, so the homomorphism is zero.

nodes.statement: The logarithmic-coordinate map H_cyc^1(χ)→E^r is an isomorphism. In particular dim_E H_cyc^1(χ)=r, and for any basis κ_i its logarithm matrix Y has nonzero determinant.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: The rational Poitou–Tate exact sequence identifies the image of global restrictions with the annihilator of the dual Kummer space U_χ; use the two local conditions from the Kummer comparison.

nodes.title: Normal form in Case 1
nodes.statement: An E-basis of W₁ is 1,π,…,π^{s−1} together with ε_J=∏_{j∈J}ε_j for every nonempty J⊆R. Its dimension is 2^r+s−1. Equivalently one may use π^s and omit ε_R. For m=(π,ε_i), π^r is nonzero in m^r/m^{r+1}.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: Reduce every monomial containing repeated ε_i or a mixed π factor to zero; all remaining monomials are powers of π and squarefree ε-products.

Use the single top relation with a≠0 to eliminate either π^s or ε_R. Define multiplication on the proposed basis by these reductions; the only overlap involving the eliminated top term multiplies it by m and both reductions give zero. Thus the reduction map is well defined and proves independence.
If s=r the surviving top line is identified with ε_R. If s>r, no relation reaches the π^r monomial in degree r+1.

nodes.title: Normal form in Case 2
nodes.statement: An E-basis of W₂ is 1,π,…,π^{s−1}, y,…,y^s and ε_J for ∅≠J⊊R. Hence dim_E W₂=2^r+2s−2. If z=π−y then z^n=π^n−y^n for n≥1; z^r has nonzero class in m^r/m^{r+1}. The entire degree-r quotient is not asserted to be one-dimensional when s>r.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: Use πy=y² to reduce mixed powers to pure y powers and the squarefree relations to remove mixed ε terms.
Since w≠0 eliminate π^s using π^s=(w+1)y^s/w, and eliminate ε_R using its nonzero top-difference relation. This works at w=−1 as well.
Construct multiplication on the indicated basis by the reduced rules; overlapping top relations annihilate m, so the reduction is associative and independent. Count the basis.
At r=s, z^r=y^s/w is a nonzero top basis element. At r<s, π^r−y^r survives modulo degree r+1 because its two pure-power terms have no relation of that degree.

nodes.title: Normal forms and two filtrations in Case 3
nodes.statement: An E-basis of W₃ is 1,π,…,π^s, y,…,y^{t−1}, and ε_J for ∅≠J⊊R; its dimension is 2^r+s+t−2. For z=π−y, z^r is nonzero in m^r/m^{r+1}. Separately, m·yW₃=y²W₃, and for 1≤n≤t the quotient y^nW₃/y^{n+1}W₃ is one-dimensional over E with generator y^n.

proofSteps: Reduce mixed πy powers using πy=y². Replace y^t by cπ^s and ε_R by its π^s multiple. Remove repeated ε and all weight-ε mixed monomials.
The reduced basis defines an associative multiplication: multiplying either top relation by m is zero, so the possible overlaps agree. This proves independence and dimension.
Since r≤t<s, the π^r term of z^r cannot enter m^{r+1}; if r=t the term y^r=cπ^s is already of higher maximal-ideal order and does not cancel it.
Multiplication of y by π or y gives y² and by ε_i gives zero. Thus y^nW₃ is spanned by y^n,…,y^t, with y^t=cπ^s≠0. Its successive quotient has precisely the indicated basis.

nodes.title: Hecke-image identification in Case 1
nodes.statement: In Case 1 the E-algebra generated by the actual Hecke action identifies with W₁. It yields a Λ-algebra homomorphism T→W₁ with T_l↦1+χε(l) for l∤np, U_l↦1 for l|n or l∈R′, and U_{q_i}↦1+ε_i.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: The leading correction and U_q stabilization identities give ε_i²=πε_i=0 and the top-product relation in W₁; the other eigenvalues follow directly from the two summands of F̃.
These relations produce a surjection W₁→φ(T)⊗_{O_E}E. Apply its proposed basis to F. Distinct π-orders separate 1,π,…,π^{s−1}.

At order s, the squarefree operators give nonzero multiples of distinct stabilized E_1(1,χ_{R′∪J}). Their q-expansions are independent: choose prime-power ideals with each possible pattern of divisibility by the q_i and use the triangular stabilization matrix. On the finite generalized Eisenstein stabilization space, t has residue eigenvalue 1 and hence acts invertibly; e is the identity there. Thus projection preserves independence as well as the fully stabilized top term. Hence the surjection is injective.

nodes.title: Hecke-image identification in Case 2

These identities give a surjection W₂→the actual image. For w≠−1, compare the leading terms of π^jF and Y^jF and then apply Y. For their coefficients α,β this gives α(1+w)+βw=0 and α+β=0 (the latter after dividing by w≠0), hence α=β=0. Proceed successively below order s.
For w=−1 begin with the order-one pair F,YF and repeat with πF,Y²F. At the last order use that Y kills the stabilized ε_JF and Y^sF but π^{s−1}YF has nonzero leading term.
The remaining stabilized Eisenstein q-expansions are independent by the prime-power triangular argument, so the basis maps injectively.

nodes.title: Hecke-image identification in Case 3
nodes.statement: In Case 3 the E-algebra generated by the actual Hecke action identifies with W₃ with the same T_l, U_l and U_{q_i} formulas as in Case 2.
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: The Case 2 action calculation does not use w≠0. The stronger identities Y^{t+1}F=0 and Y^tF=π^tWF give a surjection W₃→the actual image.
Put d=s−t≥1 and c=ν_1(W₀)≠0. The form π^jF has order j with leading E_S, while Y^iF has order d+i with leading cE_S. Also Y^tF=cπ^sF, and Y kills every nonempty ε_JF.

In a relation among the proposed basis vectors, increasing orders first removes the coefficients of π^jF for j≤d. Induct on m=1,…,t−1. Apply Y^{t−m} to the remaining relation: terms π^jF with j≥d+m vanish modulo π^{s+1}, as their order is at least 2s−t≥s+1. Terms Y^iF with i>m also vanish. The remaining term is the coefficient of Y^mF times cπ^sF, so that coefficient is zero. Comparing order d+m then kills the coefficient of π^{d+m}F.

Finally π^sF and ε_JF for proper nonempty J have independent stabilized Eisenstein leading terms by the same triangular q-expansion calculation. This fills the routine independence step left unstated in the source.

The case t=1 has no Y^i basis vectors and goes directly to the final comparison.

nodes.title: Actual Hida representations and coefficient ring
nodes.statement: Let m be the Eisenstein prime determined by T→W→E, A=T_(m) and Â its m-adic completion, with residue E. At primitive tame level (the prime-to-p conductor, with the fixed p-part retained in the character), A is a reduced Noetherian localization of the finite Λ-Hecke order, and Â is finite over the completed weight DVR; its total quotient algebra is a finite product of fields attached to actual cuspidal eigenfamilies H. For each H use the supplied continuous irreducible ρ_H:G_F→GL₂(L_H), unramified outside np, with characteristic polynomial X²−T_lX+χε(l) at l∤np and ordinary local shape [[χεη_{q,H}^{−1},*],[0,η_{q,H}]] at every q|p, where η is unramified and η(rec(ϖ^{-1}))=U_q. The product representation extends to the total quotient algebra K of Â.

The finite Hecke order and its Eisenstein congruence ideal are closed in the original Λ-adic coefficient topology before localization.
The completed reduced coefficient ring, finite over the completed weight DVR, and its total quotient injection are verified by the supplied commutative-algebra/control results.

Use the supplier’s actual irreducible family representations over finite field extensions, rather than only a pseudorepresentation or a semisimple representation over an algebraic closure.
The Frobenius coefficients and their Eisenstein congruences extend to all G_F by Chebotarev only after checking the finite-order and congruence-ideal closedness contract.
Complete at m and use its finite-field-factor decomposition; keep the injection into its total quotient algebra.

The polynomial has determinant term χε(l), not χ(l) alone.

nodes.title: Simultaneous good Galois element
nodes.statement: There exists τ∈G_F with χ(τ)≠1 such that for every field factor H and every q|p the ordinary invariant line of ρ_H|G_q is neither eigenline of ρ_H(τ). This includes the primes in R′ as well as R. The two τ-eigenvalues over the completed coefficient ring reduce to 1 and χ(τ).
hypotheses: The global arithmetic conventions of this packet apply.
proofSteps: For any line v, its stabilizer G_v is closed. If χ(G_v)≠1 and G_v had finite index, diagonalize an element of G_v with distinct residual eigenvalues. The finite off-diagonal module gives a residual cocycle whose restriction to G_v is zero.

Finite-index restriction is injective over E by averaging. In the eigenvalue order (1,χ), the lower entry is a χ-cocycle; in the reversed order use the lower entry multiplied by χ^{-1}, a χ^{-1}-cocycle. Write it as a coboundary and evaluate at the diagonal element to force its vector to zero. Nakayama kills the finite off-diagonal module, contradicting irreducibility.

A closed infinite-index subgroup of the profinite G_F has empty interior. A finite union of these cannot contain the nonempty open coset χ=χ(τ₀)≠1; intersect their open dense complements successively. Stabilizers contained in ker χ already miss that coset.
Choose τ outside the finitely many stabilizers of all ordinary lines over all q|p. Hensel lifting gives its two distinct roots.
acceptance: The source only lists q∈R in Lemma 4.3; the identical finite-avoidance argument is applied to every q|p so that the later R′ calculation has invertible local coefficients.
Only ordinary invariant lines are required; no second local eigenline is assumed to exist.

Apply the shared multiplicity-free GMA API to this actual representation. Then a,d∈Â with residues 1,χ. Let B⊆K be the finite Â-module spanned by b(σ), B̄=B/mB. The function κ(σ)=b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ) is a continuous cocycle with values in B̄(χ^{-1}); κ(τ)=0. Its class is formed in the existing continuous H^1 carrier.
